name: Imbolc

attributes.attribute: a Celtic holiday on February 1 marking the end of winter and start of spring
a Celtic goddess whose Christianized form, Saint Brigit, received the day in Ireland

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Imbolc is a Celtic holiday. It is also called Imbolg, Óilmelc, Oímelg, Olmec, or Candlemas. The Celtic year had four parts. The points between the equinoxes and solstices were major festivals. Imbolc came on February 1. On that day winter ended and spring began. Its name means in the belly. Cattle and sheep were pregnant with spring's young. It also linked to a word that means to wash. The name Óilmelc refers to the lactation of ewes. Weather magic and divination were common on the day. In Ireland the day was given to Saint Brigit. She is the Christianized form of a Celtic goddess. The Isles of Man and Britain kept their own folkways for the day.

key_results: Record its date and its place in the four-part Celtic year.
Explain the meaning of its name and the name Óilmelc.
Note the dedication of the day to Saint Brigit.
